title: no style, please! (Jekyll theme)
lede: An open-source blog theme with about 1 kB of CSS that leaves almost everything at browser defaults.
summary: riggraz’s 2020 Jekyll theme: black monospace text on white, default blue and purple underlined links, nested bullets.

evidence.note: Opened the repository’s README screenshot `_screenshots/featured-image.png` (2678 × 1500 px) with the Read tool on 2026-10-02, and read `_sass/no-style-please.scss`. Repository created 10 July 2020 (GitHub API). The live demo was not captured.

styles.note: Nearly unstyled HTML on purpose: default links, default lists, black on white, one monospace face.

context: The README describes it as “A (nearly) no-CSS, fast, minimalist Jekyll theme”, “Inspired by [elly’s site](http://tilde.town/~elly/)”, with “1kb of CSS”.
The stylesheet sets `color: black; font-family: monospace; font-size: 16px` on a white body, a 640 px column, and a dark mode made with `filter: invert(1)`. It does not set link colors.
MIT license. A Hugo port exists: [hanwenguo/hugo-theme-nostyleplease](https://github.com/hanwenguo/hugo-theme-nostyleplease) (2022).
observed: The light screenshot shows a bold monospace title, “no style, please!”, above a nested bulleted list with disc, circle, and square markers.
Links are underlined; unvisited links are bright blue and visited links purple, as in browser defaults.
Post dates in ISO form (2020-07-09) sit before each link. No images, rules, boxes, or shadows.
The dark screenshot is the same page inverted: white monospace on black, with a yellow footnote link.
interpretation: A clear current example of [Brutalist web design](style:brutalist-web-design) in the monospace variant that [NN/g (2017)](ref:nngroup-brutalism-antidesign-article-2017) describes: “blue links and monochromatic Monospace text”.
borrow: Use nested lists as navigation and let the default bullet shapes show the hierarchy.
Make a dark mode by inverting the page instead of designing a second palette.

rights.statement: The code is MIT-licensed. The screenshot was viewed at its source and is not stored.
